For fixed $m,d,n$ with $n\geq3$, the count equals \[ q^{-m}\binom{|P|}{n}(1+O_{m,d,n}(q^{1-n/2})) \] as $q\to\infty$ through admissible prime powers, uniformly over all targets and with both $p$ and $f$ allowed to vary. For fixed $m,d$, we also classify uniform relative equidistribution at the remaining positive sizes: it fails at $n=1$, and at $n=2$ it holds along an admissible sequence if and only if, for all sufficiently large terms, $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$ and $(m\geq2\text{ or }p\ne2)$.

papers.title: Kobayashi completeness of pseudoconvex domains: finite type and a smooth counterexample
papers.abstract: We prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^N$ with $C^\infty$ boundary of finite D'Angelo one-type is Kobayashi complete. As a separate consequence of our criterion of completeness and an estimate of Diederich--Fornæss, we prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain with real-analytic boundary is Kobayashi complete. We then show that smoothness alone does not imply completeness: there exists a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^3$ with $C^\infty$ boundary and a global smooth plurisubharmonic defining function whose Kobayashi and Carathéodory distances are incomplete.

papers.title: A counterexample to Gale's conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: It is known that for every partition of the sphere $S^2$ of unit diameter into four parts, the largest diameter of a part is at least $\sqrt{(3+\sqrt{3})/6} = 0.88807\dots$, and this bound is attained. The conjecture of D.~Gale (1953) asserts that no set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a larger ratio. In this paper, we construct a $101$-point set $V\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every partition of $V$ into four parts contains a part of diameter greater than $0.88928 \, \operatorname{diam} V$.

papers.title: Free boundary minimal hypersurfaces of Morse index one in Eucildean half-space
papers.abstract: We prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a half-space of RN, with nonempty boundary is a higher-dimensional half-catenoid. We also prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a quarter-space is the higher-dimensional quarter-catenoid.

papers.title: Short sums of the Möbius function over function fields
papers.abstract: We develop a new method which allows us to estimate, with a power saving, sums of the M{ö}bius function over function fields ${\mathbb F}_p(X)$. The sums run over monic polynomials with all other coefficients in short intervals, of length below the Pólya--Vinogradov threshold $p^{1/2}$. A classical result of L. Stickelberger (1898) reduces this question to bounding character sums with polynomial discriminants which are inhomogeneous multivariate polynomials. Variants of Burgess's method with non-linear shifts {\it {à} la carte} are introduced to go beyond the Pólya--Vinogradov range, combined with a stratification result of J. Xu (2020) for complete character sums.

papers.title: A Matroidal Framework for Random Access in Linear Codes
papers.abstract: We study random access in linear codes when codeword symbols are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement. A code is recovery balanced if the expected number of samples required to recover a codeword coordinate is the same for every coordinate. We express the recovery expectations in terms of the associated matroid and derive a coordinatewise identity relating these values for a code and its dual. This proves that a linear code is recovery balanced if and only if its dual is recovery balanced, establishing a conjecture of Gruica et al. We further define the recovery balance for arbitrary matroids and show that asymptotically almost every sparse paving matroid is not recovery balanced.

papers.title: Embeddings of Relative Dimension Groups for Zero-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Let $π:(X,T)\rightarrow(Y,S)$ be a factor map between zero-dimensional dynamical systems, and let $X_0$ and $Y_0$ be quasi-sections with $π(X_0)=Y_0$. We study the homomorphism $π^*:K^0(Y|Y_0,S)\rightarrow K^0(X|X_0,T)$, $[f]\mapsto[f\circπ]$, between the corresponding relative dimension groups, and identify it with the homomorphism induced by the premorphism between Bratteli--Vershik realizations associated with $π$. Generalizing a result of Glasner and Weiss for minimal Cantor systems, we show that if $Y_0$ is quasi-simple, then $π^*$ is an injective unital order-preserving homomorphism, and that if $X_0=π^{-1}(Y_0)$, then $π^*$ is a unital order embedding; the latter condition is characterized in terms of the premorphism. Examples show that quasi-simplicity cannot be dropped, and that without the condition $X_0=π^{-1}(Y_0)$ the map $π^*$ need not be an order embedding.

papers.title: The moduli space of maps from hypersurfaces and its Goodwillie tower
papers.abstract: We define a moduli space of continuous maps from smooth hypersurfaces varying in an ample linear system. To study its topology, we construct a scanning map to an appropriate section space and investigate its effect on homology. Our main innovation is a general argument based on Goodwillie calculus and applicable to various moduli spaces of maps. Along the way, we compute the Goodwillie tower of the section space functor based at any retractive space.

papers.title: Deflation-Based Spectral Preconditioning for the Conjugate Gradient Method on Perturbed Systems
papers.abstract: We consider sequences of large symmetric positive-definite linear systems in which spectral information from a reference matrix $A$ is reused to accelerate the solution of a nearby system with perturbed matrix $A(t)=A+tE$, where $E$ is symmetric, $\|E\|_F=1$, and $t\geq0$ is the perturbation size. We compare deflated conjugate gradient (deflated CG) with preconditioned CG (PCG) equipped with a scaled spectral preconditioner constructed from the same spectral information of $A$. First, we derive an energy-norm error characterization of deflated CG. We then use perturbation analysis to show that, after one additional PCG iteration, the squared PCG error is bounded, up to terms of order $t^2$, by an explicit multiple of the squared deflated CG error. This result clarifies the role of the scaling parameter in the preconditioner. Experiments show that the scaled spectral preconditioner recovers much of the convergence improvement provided by deflation while requiring fewer products with $A(t)$.

papers.title: Closedness of bounded strength and partition rank loci
papers.abstract: We show the existence of a quartic form of strength $3$ in the closure of the strength at most $2$ locus, answering a question of Ballico--Bik--Oneto--Ventura in the negative. In the analogous setting of partition rank as introduced by Naslund, we further show that the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $2$ is closed, but the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $3$ is not. Together with a suspension lemma, this answers for all $r$ whether the locus of forms/tensors of strength/partition rank at most $r$ is Zariski-closed.

papers.title: Spherically Supported Sets with Variable Radii
papers.abstract: We study closed sets for which, at every boundary point, there exists a containing supporting ball whose prescribed radius may vary from point to point. This extends the notion of spherical support from constant to variable radii. The variable-radius setting presents a new difficulty: unlike the constant-radius case, the intersection of the supporting balls need not be strongly convex with respect to the prescribed radii. We overcome this difficulty by associating with every such set a canonical set and an induced radius function determined by the active supporting balls. For continuous prescribed radii, our main result establishes a geometric dichotomy: the original set either coincides with the canonical set and is strongly convex with respect to the prescribed radii, or it is contained in the boundary of the canonical set, which is strongly convex with respect to the induced radii. An example shows that the induced radii cannot, in general, be replaced by the prescribed ones in the second alternative. We also recover the constant-radius theory and characterize variable-radius strong convexity in terms of the spherical support of the boundary.

papers.title: A relative Schinzel-Zassenhaus bound for the polynomial $T^2 - 1$
papers.abstract: For $f(T) = T^2 - 1$, we establish a lower bound for the relative dynamical house of wandering algebraic integers. This bound depends on the degree over the maximal abelian extension of the rationals. Our proof follows Dimitrov's approach to the Schinzel-Zassenhaus Conjecture and its generalization by Habegger-Schmidt.

papers.title: Low-degree filtrations in ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology
papers.abstract: We prove the Hilbert-series formulas conjectured by Reiner--Tudose and by the Polymath Jr. Grassmannian group for the subalgebras of ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology generated in bounded degree. We determine the finite coefficient images underlying the proofs, together with the kernels of the coefficient and cancellation maps. We also construct bases adapted to the auxiliary ideal filtrations and identify the cancellation layers, as modules, with shifts of finite complete-intersection algebras. First-order deformations give the derivative inclusions needed to recover the filtration increments. We disprove the two ordinary basis conjectures of the Polymath group. For every $r\ge 2$, the span of each prescribed family has codimension one in weight $3r+2$ of $H^{2*}(\operatorname{Gr}(2,3r+1);\mathbb Q)$; replacing one index gives a basis in each of these components. More generally, each prescribed two-row family has codimension at most one in every weight. Weights are half the cohomological degrees, and all coefficients are rational.

papers.title: A quaternary Diophantine inequality with prime numbers of a special form (II)
papers.abstract: Let $N$ be a sufficiently large real number. In this paper, it is proved that, for $1<c<\frac{5179}{3909}$ and for any arbitrary large number $E>0$, the Diophantine inequality \begin{equation*} \big|p_1^c+p_2^c+p_3^c+p_4^c-N\big|<(\log N)^{-E} \end{equation*} is solvable in prime variables $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ such that each of the numbers $p_i+2\,(i=1,2,3,4)$ has, counted according to multiplicity, at most $[\frac{31250}{5179-3909c}]$ prime factors, which constitutes a large improvement upon the previous results of Dimitrov [13] and Li-Xue-Zhang [22], respectively.

papers.title: Schäffer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$
papers.abstract: In 1956, Schäffer made a conjecture on the whole number solutions to the Diophantine equation $S_k(x):=1^k+2^k+\cdots+x^k=y^n$. In this paper we show how for even $k$, we can descend to a long list of three coupled equations of the form $Ax^p-By^p=1$, where $A,B\in\mathbb{Q}$. To this system, we apply the modular method, linear forms in logarithms, and local methods. As a result, we prove Schäffer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$.

papers.title: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
papers.abstract: We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$. On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge11$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.

papers.title: Sharp quantitative stability of the Hong--Krahn--Szegő inequality
papers.abstract: We establish sharp quantitative stability estimates for the Hong--Krahn--Szegő inequality for arbitrary open sets of positive finite measure in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. In dimensions $d\ge3$, the optimal stability exponent is $(d+2)/2$, while in dimension two the sharp stability modulus is $t^2/\log(e/t)$. These results improve the quantitative stability estimate of Brasco and Pratelli~\cite[Theorem 3.5]{BP} and resolve Open Problem 7.56 of Brasco and De Philippis~\cite[Open Problem 7.56]{BDP}.

papers.title: Outer automorphisms of HNN extensions of abelian groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a commensurating HNN extension of a finitely generated free abelian group. We characterise when $\mathrm{Out}(G)$ is finitely generated and derive structural information about the group. We give soluble and non-soluble examples of commensurating HNN extensions of finitely generated free abelian groups with outer automorphism group not finitely generated.

papers.title: Measures of maximal entropy for meromorphic maps on compact Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact Kähler manifold. Assume that $f$ has a strictly dominant intermediate dynamical degree $λ$ and that the number of isolated $n$-periodic points, counted with multiplicity, is at most $λ^n+o(λ^n)$. Then $f$ admits at most one adapted invariant probability measure of entropy $\logλ$. If such a measure exists, its natural extension is Bernoulli, and the isolated periodic points equidistribute towards it when counted with or without multiplicity. We apply this criterion to several classes of maps in complex dynamics, resolving longstanding open problems.

papers.title: Low-Dimensional Reduction of Mean-Field Coupled Dynamical Systems with Units Described by Two Real Variables: Classification and Applications
papers.abstract: Low-dimensional reduction is crucial for understanding network systems with many units. In a recent advance, Martens and Dharmavaram developed a theory of exact low-dimensional reduction for a general class of mean-field coupled dynamical systems characterized by a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure. In this paper, we classify mean-field coupled dynamical systems with a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, where each unit is described by two real variables. Our classification is based on González-López, Kamran, and Olver's local classification of Lie systems on the plane near generic points and yields 28 types of mean-field coupled dynamical systems. For mean-field coupled systems with units described by two real variables, we first present a general theory on classification and low-dimensional reduction based on the mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, and then discuss applications to populations of coupled oscillators. We show that low-dimensional reduction is possible for a broad class of populations of limit-cycle oscillators, extending the previously reported reducible class of populations of Stuart-Landau oscillators to include many new models.

papers.title: Singular solutions to the complex Monge-Ampère equation II
papers.abstract: Continuing our work in [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 1503-1518], we construct new singular solutions to the complex Monge-Ampère equation with constant right-hand side in the Bedford-Taylor sense. Let $\mathbb D$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb C$. For $n\geq 2$, these solutions include: (i) a bounded solution on $\mathbb D^n$ that is discontinuous almost everywhere and nowhere classically differentiable; (ii) a continuous exhaustion of $\mathbb C^n$ that does not belong to $W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb C^n)$; (iii) a continuous solution on $\overline{\mathbb D^n}$ whose Laplacian has a singular part. We construct these solutions from singular harmonic functions using partial Legendre transforms and holomorphic pullbacks.

papers.title: Generic finiteness of solutions to parametrized systems of generalized polynomial inequalities
papers.abstract: We study parametrized systems of $\mathit{generalized}$ polynomial inequalities, $(c \circ x^B) \in C$, for a positive variable vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^n_>$, a $\mathit{real}$ exponent matrix $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}$, a positive parameter vector $c \in \mathbb{R}^m_>$, and a positive, blunt coefficient cone $C \subset \mathbb{R}^m_>$. This setting includes (i) generalized polynomial equations, $A \, (c \circ x^B) = 0$, arising e.g. from power-law dynamical systems with real exponents (and involving a real coefficient matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n' \times m}$), and (ii) generalized semi-algebraic sets. Our main result guarantees the generic finiteness of solutions modulo unavoidable exponential fibers. Building on a framework for parametrized $\mathit{polynomial}$ systems developed by Müller and Regensburger, we reformulate the problem as a system of $\mathit{binomial}$ equations on the coefficient set $P = C \cap Δ\subseteq \mathbb{R}^m_>$, where $Δ$ is a product of (standard) simplices. Solvability is governed by the monomial-dependency subspace $D$. Using elementary arguments from analysis and topology, including a logarithmic boundary analysis and Sard's theorem, we control the accumulation of solutions on the boundary and in the interior of $P$. We show that, if $\dim P \le \dim D$, then generically in both the measure-theoretic and topological sense, there are finitely many solutions on $P$ (and hence finitely many exponential fibers of solutions in $\mathbb{R}^n_>$). As an application, we prove generic finiteness of steady states (within forward-invariant sets) for parametrized power-law dynamical systems with real exponents.

papers.title: Birthday Estimators Are Uniformly Optimal for Renyi Entropy
papers.abstract: Collisions are a basic probe of unknown distributions, used for testing and for counting substructures in graphs, and they underlie Rényi entropy, a fundamental measure of uncertainty with applications in cryptography, machine learning, physics, and biology. Motivated by this, we study the natural birthday estimator. We prove Bernstein-type concentration for it and show that it is minimax optimal, uniformly and jointly in alphabet size, order, accuracy, and confidence, with no sample splitting, clipping, or median aggregation. This, in particular, settles the sample complexity of integer-order Rényi entropy estimation up to absolute constants in all regimes, closing the gap between the best known upper and lower bounds. Our concentration bound rests on a sensitivity analysis of collision count, and the matching lower bound on a sharp analysis of detecting a hidden spike in a plateau distribution.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Policy Gradient from Discrete Data: Convergence Analysis and Model-Free Algorithms
papers.abstract: Continuous-time reinforcement learning seeks an optimal policy under unknown dynamics driven by stochastic differential equations using observations collected at discrete times. We develop a policy gradient framework that combines rigorous convergence analysis with learning from discrete data. We first establish a performance difference lemma and derive policy gradient formulas for randomized and parametrized policies. We then prove exponential convergence of an entropy-regularized policy flow to the regularized optimum. For discrete parametrized updates, we derive a convergence bound that explicitly separates the contributions of critic error, policy-regression error, and the learning step size. To enable learning under unknown dynamics, we integrate this framework with PhiBE, which constructs a continuous-time surrogate generator from discrete transition data. The resulting on-policy and off-policy model-free actor-critic algorithms preserve the continuous-time structure of the control problem. Numerical experiments on an entropy-regularized linear-quadratic regulator and a nonlinear wheeled robot demonstrate the performance and stability of the proposed methods with both known and data-driven dynamics.

papers.title: Vanishing Uniform Turán Densities: Characterization and Jumps
papers.abstract: Uniform Turán density problems ask for the minimum density threshold that guarantees a copy of a fixed 3-uniform hypergraph $F$ in every sufficiently large 3-uniform hypergraph whose edges are uniformly distributed. This line of research was initiated by Erdős and Sós in the 1980s, who introduced the notion of \emph{vertex-set Turán density} $π_{vvv}(F)$. Reiher, Rödl and Schacht later defined two related concepts, namely, the \emph{vertex-pair Turán density} $π_{ve}(F)$ and the \emph{cherry Turán density} $π_{ee}(F)$, which satisfy the chain of inequalities $π_{vvv}(F)\geπ_{ve}(F)\geπ_{ee}(F)$. In this paper, we investigate the problem for their vanishing densities. First, we characterize the 3-uniform hypergraphs $F$ for which $π_{ee}(F)=0$, thereby answering a question posed by Schacht. We show that these are precisely the so-called \emph{max-layered} 3-uniform hypergraphs recently introduced by Lamaison. Furthermore, we answer an analogous question of Lamaison for the \emph{minimum-codegree palette density} $π_{ee}^{\rm pal}$. Together, these results imply that the following are equivalent: $π_{ee}(F)=0$, $π_{ee}^{\rm pal}(F)=0$, and $F$ is a max-layered 3-uniform hypergraph. Let $\star \in \{vvv, ve, ee \}$. We say that zero is a \emph{jump} for $π_{\star}$ if there exists $c>0$ such that no $3$-uniform hypergraph $F$ satisfies $π_{\star}(F)\in(0,c)$. A famous result of Reiher, Rödl and Schacht asserts that zero is a jump for $π_{vvv}$. In contrast, we prove that zero is not a jump for either $π_{ve}$ or $π_{ee}$. This also yields a negative answer to Schacht's well-ordering question for $π_{ve}$. Together with existing results, these findings complete the picture for all three notions of uniform Turán density at zero.

papers.title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
papers.abstract: In this work, we establish existence and regularity results for solutions to nonlinear nonlocal equations of the form $f(Δ)u = U(x,u)$ and $f(Δ_{g})u = U(x,u)$ in Euclidean and Riemannian settings, respectively. We prove existence results across three distinct geometric scenarios: bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, perturbed equations on compact Riemannian manifolds, and noncompact Cartan-Hadamard manifolds under suitable geometric curvature conditions.

papers.title: The Dynamics of Collapse and Recovery in Clustered Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Clustered federated learning (CFL) can suffer from cluster collapse. In particular, under unfavorable initialization, early client assignments concentrate heterogeneous groups on one cluster model, which is then trained toward a pooled compromise, while another model receives no updates. Since the current models determine client routing and routing determines subsequent model updates, we formulate clustered federated learning as control of an unknown dynamical system, with cluster models as the evolving state, client routing patterns as the control input, and routing interventions as state dependent controllers. In a two group linear model, we identify an initialization region in which greedy routing makes collapse self reinforcing. We then derive finite horizon error dynamics showing how routing interventions can reverse collapse by repeatedly training the starved model, primarily with updates from its compatible group. Motivated by this condition, each client uses blocked EXP3 to choose between greedy routing and interventions that redirect updates toward unused models. Experiments show that with simpler predictors and faster specialist formation, autonomous controller selection recovers usable specialists from unfavorable starts that trap standard CFL baselines. In transformed FEMNIST, the synchronized-entry configuration with persistent commitment recovers usable specialists in settings where the autonomous controller configuration often does not. Code and scripts for reproducing the experiments and figures are available at https://github.com/prsinha1/FedRecover.

papers.title: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws
papers.abstract: Many scientific phenomena are best understood as outcomes of underlying optimization problems, yet automated scientific discovery has largely focused on recovering equations that describe observed input-output patterns. We introduce OptScientist, a novel automated framework for discovering compact symbolic optimization laws directly from data. OptScientist comprises (i) a model that infers symbolic optimization problems by first learning to represent data as an optimization problem and then extracting its symbolic form, and (ii) an LLM agentic system embedding the model in a discovery process that integrates theoretical priors from scientific literature, discovers candidate laws, abstracts their underlying mechanisms, and suggests new data to collect. We first evaluate OptScientist on OptFeynman, a novel benchmark of 99 physics-derived optimization problems, where OptScientist recovers ground-truth laws for over 80% of the problems and remains robust to noisy contextual information, while substantially outperforming machine-learning, symbolic, and LLM-based model-discovery baselines. On human risky choice and central-bank monetary policy, OptScientist discovers compact symbolic optimization laws that achieve held-out predictive performance competitive with leading baselines, while using few parameters and substantially fewer tokens than LLM baselines. Overall, OptScientist extends automated scientific discovery to uncovering optimization laws that generate observed phenomena, enabling automated theory building across the physical, biological, behavioral, and social sciences.

papers.title: Convergence of stochastic gradient descent for learning linear neural networks
papers.abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is the cornerstone of modern deep learning, yet its theoretical convergence properties remain poorly understood in non-convex settings. To address this gap, we study SGD dynamics in deep linear neural networks - simplified models that retain key non-convex characteristics while remaining analytically tractable. Building on recent results for gradient descent, we extend convergence guarantees to SGD under regularized squared loss. We establish almost sure boundedness of SGD iterates. Using the framework of asymptotic pseudotrajectories from stochastic approximation theory, our analysis establishes then, for both deterministic and adaptive step-size choices, convergence of SGD to the set of critical points under mild conditions (without relying on Lipschitz properties or whitened data). To our knowledge, this is the first work providing almost sure convergence guarantees for SGD in deep linear networks, bridging the gap between theoretical optimization and practical stochastic training.

papers.title: Higher-order tangent lines to smooth hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that for every smooth hypersurface $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d\geq n \geq 5$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the space of pointed lines $(\ell,p)$ having intersection multiplicity at least six with $X$ at $p$ has the expected dimension $2n-7$. The proof uses deformations of ruled surfaces preserving prescribed contact with $X$. As an application, we show that a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\geq 6$ in $\mathbb{P}^5$ contains at most $225d^3-1370d^2+1800d$ planes. This bound has optimal order of growth in $d$.

papers.title: A Statistical Imaging Framework for Inverse Obstacle Scattering and Its Resolution Analysis
papers.abstract: We develop a general statistical framework for inverse obstacle imaging and resolution analysis from far-field second moments under random illumination. The regularized $Q$-statistic is introduced and utilized to measure the minimal statistically weighted cost of synthesizing the test far field associated with a sampling point. Its reciprocal provides an imaging indicator. Under uniform full-aperture plane-wave illumination, we relate this indicator to several classical sampling indicators and derive their statistical counterparts for general random illumination. For the resolution analysis, separating the effects of radiation and noise from the statistics of induced boundary sources, we measure a correlation-free resolution limit by the one-sided half-height width of the boundary transition. In the regime of fixed wavenumber $k$ with the noise-calibrated regularization level $ρ_τ\to 0$, we establish a sharp asymptotic law for this width for simply connected domains with analytic boundaries. The width scales as \(h_Γ(x)\log\log(1/ρ_τ)/\log(1/ρ_τ)\), with $h_Γ(x)$ a geometric prefactor along the boundary determining both the boundary image contrast and the local transition width. For general boundary-source statistics, we examine how the source mean, variance, and correlation affect imaging quality. Finally, in representative scattering configurations, we provide qualitative interpretations of some typical imaging phenomena through the statistical structure of their induced boundary sources. Numerical examples illustrate these mechanisms and indicate that practical resolution is governed jointly by source statistics, radiation, the noise level, rather than by wavelength alone.

papers.title: Strong Convergence of Fully Discrete Tamed Euler Approximations for Time-Changed Stochastic Delay Differential Equations
papers.abstract: We establish the strong convergence of a fully discrete equidistant tamed Euler--Maruyama (ETEM) method for time-changed stochastic delay differential equations (TCSDDEs) with state-dependent $\mathrm{d}t$ drifts. A coupled one-sided condition on the subordinator-driven drift and diffusion allows superlinear coefficients with polynomial growth in both the current and delayed states. For subordinators whose Laplace exponent satisfies $ψ(λ)\geq c_1λ^α$ for all sufficiently large $λ$, with $α\in(0,1)$, we derive strong error bounds in terms of the time step $Δ$ and the subordinator sampling step $δ$, without imposing a relationship between them. Comparing the partitions generated by the exact and approximate inverse subordinators controls the sampling error without introducing a factor proportional to the number of time steps. For coefficients Lipschitz in both time arguments and Lipschitz history, the scheme achieves a strong convergence rate of order $Δ^{α/2}(1+|\logΔ|)^{(1-α)/2}+\sqrt{δ(1+|\logδ|)}$. A terminal lower bound $c(Δ^{α/2}+δ^{1/2})$ for a multiplicative-noise equation with a stable subordinator establishes the sharpness of both polynomial exponents for this Euler scheme. Numerical experiments illustrate convergence for nonautonomous and multidimensional superlinear delay equations, as well as delay equations with low-regularity time dependence.

papers.title: Cutoff profile for the balanced generalized Bernoulli--Laplace model
papers.abstract: We study the balanced generalized Bernoulli--Laplace model introduced by Goenka, Hermon, and Schmid (2025) and establish a Gaussian cutoff profile under spectral conditions satisfied by all reversible chains and the cyclic shift chain. Our method adapts the approach of Olesker-Taylor and Schmid (2026) for the two-urn model, combining concentration around a deterministic trajectory before the cutoff window with an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck approximation near equilibrium. We also give an instance of this model that exhibits cutoff but has no limit profile. Further, we determine the mixing time up to an additive constant for every irreducible instance of the model, identifying a $\log \log n$ correction governed by the largest Jordan block size corresponding to the slowest decaying modes.

papers.title: Local well-posedness of wave kinetic equations associated with water waves
papers.abstract: We prove two conceptually different local well-posedness results for wave kinetic equations associated with water-wave systems. For pure gravity waves with 2D interfaces, we establish a classical well-posedness theory in weighted Sobolev spaces: regularity is propagated, and solutions depend continuously on the initial data in the same topology. For gravity-capillary waves with one-dimensional interfaces, the situation is fundamentally different. We prove well-posedness in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces (in the sense of existence, uniqueness, and continuity in a weaker topology), but we also show that, in general, any additional regularity of the initial data is instantly lost. Moreover, continuity in time and continuous dependence on the initial data fail in the weighted $L^\infty$ norm, even for smooth compactly supported initial data. This instability is caused by degenerate three-wave resonances, which produce singular collision rates and arbitrarily short relaxation time scales. The distinction between the two theories reflects a fundamental difference in their resonant geometry.

papers.title: Local crystallization in three-dimensional quantization
papers.abstract: A long-standing conjecture on the quantization problem due to Gersho, which remains open in dimensions higher than two, posits that optimal quantizers crystallize into a lattice structure; in dimension three, the natural candidate is the body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, known to be optimal among other lattices. In this paper, we establish the asymptotic local optimality of the BCC lattice under small periodic perturbations, extending its known stability beyond the class of lattice configurations. Our approach connects the discrete geometry of Voronoi tessellations with a continuum variational problem, showing that the rescaled quadratic quantization energies converge to a continuum functional describing locally deformed BCC lattices. A central ingredient is a geometric and algebraic framework that combines the stability of the BCC Voronoi structure, a discrete calculus on its adjacency graph and an analysis of the lattice symmetries via representation theory, allowing us to establish the positivity of the second variation at the BCC configuration and thereby prove the local minimality of the BCC lattice for the limiting energy.

papers.title: On Nonlocal Equations under Symmetries
papers.abstract: In this work, we establishes results of existence and regularity for solutions to nonlocal equations of the form $f(Δ)u = U(x,u(x)) ~\text{and}~f(Δ_{g})u=U(x,u(x))$ in the Euclidean context and Riemannian context respectively. We extend the results of \cite{Gorka 6} for the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ under cylindrically symmetry and compact Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ under action of a closed Lie subgroup $G \leq \text{Isom}_{g}(M)$. Our approach combines spectral theory, complex interpolation and fixed-point methods.

papers.title: New Newton-type inequality and a unified perspective on Maclaurin's inequality via the inclusion relations of cones
papers.abstract: The classical Newton-Maclaurin's inequalities for the elementary symmetric means are well known. In this paper, we derive a new class of Newton-type inequalities and generalize Maclaurin's inequality by connecting the elementary symmetric functions with their counterparts. Our idea is mainly motivated by the inclusion relations of G$\mathring{\text{a}}$rding's cones and $k$-convex cones.

papers.title: Extremal secant size distributions in projective planes
papers.abstract: Given a point set $S$ in a projective plane of order $q$, each line $\ell$ determines a secant of size $|S\cap \ell|$. We study how concentrated this secant-size distribution can be. We develop a general framework for estimating and, in several cases, determining the extremal number. We point out how the extremal constructions vary depending on the remainder of the size of the set modulo $q$, and classify several extremal families of point sets, building from concurrent lines, Baer {subplanes} and lines in general position. On the lower bound side, we rely on stability results in the Desarguesian case and applications of the standard equalities in general. Finally, we connect the problem to a novel concept, called general position on level 2 for point and line sets, which then leads to a Sidon-type problem over finite fields called projective Sidon sets, providing an additional arithmetic model for highly concentrated secant-size distributions.

papers.title: A sharp bound on the binding number of $K_k$-free graphs and the Brandt conjecture
papers.abstract: The binding number of a graph is the smallest ratio $|N(S)|/|S|$ among all nonempty vertex sets $S$ whose neighborhood $N(S)$ is not the whole vertex set. We prove that every finite nonempty $K_k$-free graph has binding number at most $k-2$ for every $k\ge6$, confirming Brandt's conjecture; the bound is sharp for complete $(k-1)$-partite graphs with equal nonempty parts. We first prove the case $k=6$ and then extend it to all $k\ge6$ by induction.

papers.title: 2-representation theory of the Taft algebra
papers.abstract: We study the $2$-representation theory of the Taft category, the tensor category of finite-dimensional modules over the Taft algebra. This category has two left cells. We first classify suitable transitive modules over its based representation ring. For the upper cell, we recall a construction by Etingof and Ostrik giving an infinite family of pairwise nonequivalent simple $2$-representations. For the bottom cell, we pass to the semisimplification of the Taft category and identify a distinguished fusion subcategory with an adjoint $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Verlinde category. Using algebra objects associated with $\mathsf{ADET}$-diagrams and categorical Clifford theory, we classify the regular exact indecomposable module categories of this semisimplification. For these regular module categories, the split Grothendieck group is a complete invariant. Finally, we identify the two cell $2$-representations of the Taft category.

papers.title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
papers.abstract: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $δ^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{δ+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,Δ}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $Δ(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $δ+1={\rm deg}\,Δ$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.

papers.title: Small and large gaps between zeros of Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: For every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove unconditionally that infinitely many consecutive zeros have spacing less than $1/2+\varepsilon$ times the mean. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we also prove a positive proportion of such spacings for the Riemann zeta-function, and infinitely many spacings greater than $3.63$ times the mean for every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function.

papers.title: The $λ>0$ case for $Δu=λ-c e^u$ type equation on high dimensional spheres
papers.abstract: Motivated by prescribed Chern scalar curvature problems in complex geometry, we study the equation $Δ_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}V+λ(e^V-1)=0$ with $λ>0$ on spheres. For $N\ge4$ and $λ>2(N-2)$ with $λ\ne2N$, we prove the existence of a nonconstant smooth solution that is axially symmetric and symmetric about the equator.

papers.title: Variance Reduction with Delayed Feedback for Non-Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study variance reduction for non-convex optimization when gradient evaluations return with a delay. The server can update the parameter while earlier evaluations remain unfinished. We first analyze an ordered recursive momentum estimator for stochastic optimization. Under average smoothness and bounded variance, its oracle complexity is $O(1+σ^2ε^{-2}+LΔ_f(1+σ/ε+τ)ε^{-2})$, where the target is an expected squared gradient norm of at most $ε^2$ and $τ$ bounds the feedback delay. We next study finite sums with $n$ components and obtain $O(n+LΔ_f(\sqrt n+\min\{τ,n-1\})ε^{-2})$ evaluations. An asynchronous snapshot variant continues updating during full-gradient computations under an explicit bound on their completion time. For the stochastic method, we further replace a maximum-delay bound by a bound on the weighted amount of missing feedback.

papers.title: An exact formula for optimal axis-parallel packing of eight squares
papers.abstract: We determine the smallest square container for eight axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths. The optimal side length is the minimum of the costs of 23 explicit packing strategies, and each cost is a maximum of sums of side lengths. No minimum of fewer convex functions represents it. Three strategies suffice for seven squares; the jump to 23 for eight squares witnesses the beginning of a combinatorial explosion. We prove the formula by combining the constructions with geometric lower bounds derived from disjoint coordinate projections, cornering arguments, and a weighted area comparison.

papers.title: Extremals for Sharp Trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev Inequalities on Convex Cones
papers.abstract: Zugmeyer~\cite{Zug} established sharp trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequalities on convex cones for $a\geq n>p>1$. We classify all nonzero real-valued extremals of these inequalities. Let the cone be the epigraph of a finite convex function that is positively homogeneous of degree one, and let $H$ be any norm. We prove that equality holds precisely for functions of the form $A H(x+te+\ell)^{-(a-p)/(p-1)}$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\}$, $t>0$, $e=(0,\ldots,0,1)$, and $\ell$ belongs to the largest vector subspace contained in the cone. The result includes the critical Sobolev trace inequality at $a=n$, as well as nonsmooth norms and cones, half-spaces, and cones containing lines.

papers.title: Quadratic hulls of osculating varieties of rational normal curves
papers.abstract: Let $T^p c_r$ be the $p$-osculating variety of the rational normal curve $c_r\subset\mathbb{P}S^r(\mathbb{C}^2)$. We study its quadratic hull, the scheme defined by the quadratic equations vanishing on $T^p c_r$. For $r\ge2p+3$, we prove that this scheme is a complete intersection of $\binom{r-2p}{2}$ quadrics whenever \[ p\ge\binom{r-2p-1}{2}. \] When the inequality is strict, the hull is integral and strictly contains $T^p c_r$. On the boundary its support is reducible, except for $(p,r)=(1,5)$, where the hull equals the osculating variety. The proof is local at the highest weight point. Koornwinder's relation between Clebsch--Gordan coefficients and Hahn polynomials leads to a description of the tangent-cone equations in which each antidiagonal becomes an ordinary polynomial space of bounded degree. An incidence estimate then gives a normal integral tangent cone in the strict range, and the $SL_2$-action turns this local statement into global integrality.

papers.title: Christoffel transformations of symmetric $d$-connections and gap probability recurrences
papers.abstract: We study the Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ of an even discrete weight. For the associated orthogonal polynomial ensembles on squared nodes $y=x^2$, ratios of moment determinants relate the largest-particle distributions and transfer exact gap probability recurrences between the ensembles. For positive weights satisfying the stated moment and support assumptions, this comparison requires no Pearson condition. The transformation is realized by elementary bundle modifications at zero and infinity on $\mathbb P^1$. When the original weight has Pearson ratio $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\mathrm{deg}\; d=1,2$, these modifications conjugate cutoff dynamics on common stable loci of symmetric $d$-connections under the stated geometric hypotheses. The transformed recurrence coefficients are expressed explicitly as rational functions of spectral coordinates. On the unit lattice, a local recurrence formula applies to rational symmetric Pearson ratios of arbitrary degree, including outside these charts, whenever its local hypotheses hold.

papers.title: Photonic band structure by direct second-kind free-space boundary integral equations
papers.abstract: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via Müller's formulation. The wall equations, in turn, come from a stack formulation, in which Green's formula is applied on stacks of three cells, so that the wall self-interactions and the interactions between arcs sharing endpoints cancel exactly. The resulting system is of the second kind, Fredholm of index zero, and free of corner singularities, and the walls may be curved to keep the cell boundary away from the inclusions. Its operators are assembled once per frequency and reused for all Bloch vectors. We prove that every Bloch mode yields a nonzero null vector, and that a null vector comes from a Bloch mode exactly when its cell representation vanishes outside the cell, which gives an inexpensive test for spurious null vectors. The band frequencies are computed with a high-order Nyström discretization and the search of Bruno, Santana and Trefethen, which locates them as poles of adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) rational approximants to a randomly scalarized resolvent sampled on the real frequency axis. Numerical examples validate the method against exact and published band structures and include a challenging triangular lattice of air pores in a dielectric, whose cell requires curved walls.

papers.title: Discrete Exterior Calculus-based Whittle-Matérn Fields on Meshes
papers.abstract: This work presents a sparse precision formulation for Whittle-Matérn fields based on Discrete Exterior Calculus. By treating the $k$-cochain as the latent object to be modeled, we show that a single formulation can produce Whittle-Matérn fields for all $k$ and integer $α$ values. By utilising Whitney maps we can enable a push-forward of the prior on 1-cochains, enabling inference for discrete vector fields. We demonstrate this model on interpolation of vector fields on a sphere.

papers.title: Liouville Theorems for Semilinear Parabolic Equations Involving the Nonlinear Gradient Term
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^q$ via the integral Bernstein method, where $q=2p/(p+1)$ is critical and $M<0$. As an application, we can establish a universal priori estimate for this equation by using the doubling lemma. These results generalize the previous work of Liang and Zhang. We can also prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^2$, which corresponds to the supercritical case.

papers.title: A single generation theorem for simple unital $C^*$-algebras with CPoU and comparison
papers.abstract: In this note, assuming the finite factor generation theorem obtained by OpenAI, we demonstrate that if a separable simple unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ with nonempty trace space, has the strict comparison for positive elements, and its uniform tracial completion has complemented partitions of unity (CPoU), then $A$ is singly generated.

papers.title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications
papers.abstract: We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.

papers.title: On the Geometry of Low Rank Correlation Matrices
papers.abstract: Correlation matrices of bounded rank form a stratified space whose factor representations lie in a product of spheres. Using the orbit-type description of the rank stratification, we prove that padding factors preserves the Riemannian geometry of each fixed-rank stratum and the intrinsic length metric of every rank-bounded subset. In the reduced model, a Sylvester equation describes the mechanical connection and its horizontal lifts. We derive sectional-curvature formulas and bounds, characterize zero-curvature directions, and determine the connection's holonomy groups. In particular, a flat rank-two connection can have nontrivial dihedral holonomy. For geodesics subject to a rank bound, rank cannot decrease in the interior of a minimizing segment with maximal-rank endpoints; the local excess over the unconstrained quotient distance is controlled by a dimension-independent cubic estimate. Finally, we compute the exact change of measure between quotient Riemannian volume and Euclidean surface volume in the off-diagonal entries. Coarea yields explicit factor densities for both normalized uniform laws.

papers.title: C*-selflessness and $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for Thompson's group $F$
papers.abstract: We prove that the reduced C*-algebra of Thompson's group $F$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless.

papers.title: On the stability of displacement energy in toric manifolds
papers.abstract: We present a quantitative exploration of the behaviour of displacement energy of Lagrangians under stabilization. In particular, we completely characterize the displacement behaviour of toric fibres in Fano 4-manifolds. Our approach relates the geometry of the moment polytope's caustic to the structure of the (bulk-deformed) superpotential and to the presence of symmetric probes.

papers.title: Independent transversals in hypergraphs with low codegrees
papers.abstract: We prove that for every fixed $r\geq3$, $k>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there is $γ>0$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $b$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ whose vertex set is partitioned into parts of size at least $b$ contains at least $\lceil(1-\varepsilon)b\rceil$ pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals, provided that the average degree in each part is at most $kb^{r-1}$ and maximum $j$-codegree $Δ_j(\mathcal H)\leqγb^{r-j}$ for $2\leq j<r$. Under the same average degree, if $q$ is the minimum part size and $Δ_j(\mathcal H)=o(q^{r-j})$ for $2\leq j<r$, the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals is $(1-o(1))q$ as $q\to\infty$. We develop an iterative halving reduction for partitioned hypergraphs to apply the theorem of Delcourt and Postle on matchings avoiding forbidden submatchings.

papers.title: ACM, almost Ulrich, and Ulrich vector bundles arising from Frobenius
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We investigate ACM, almost Ulrich (both ACM and weakly Ulrich), and Ulrich properties of the sheaves of locally exact and closed $i$-forms $B_X^i$, $Z_X^i$. These cohomological properties are closely related to the fundamental concepts of Frobenius splitting and ordinarity. Joshi studied the sheaf $B^1_X$ in this context in \cite{MR3920911, MR4206787}, including ACM and almost Ulrich twists of $B^1_X$. However, varieties with Ulrich twisted $B_X^1$ have not been classified for $n\ge2$. We classify subcanonical polarized varieties with initialized ACM $B^i_X(aH)$ for $i=1, n$ and prove that, for $n \ge 2$, varieties with ACM $B^i_X$ for all $i \le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$ are ordinary. When $X$ is ordinary with trivial $Ω^1_X$, almost Ulrich twists of $B^i_X$ and $F_*^e(Z_X^i(aH))$ are determined. We classify polarized varieties $(X,H)$ with $B_X^i(aH)$ Ulrich when $n=1, 2$, and establish strong necessary criteria for $n \geq 3$, together with an example. We also prove that $Z_X^i(aH)$ is never Ulrich. Finally, we classify polarized abelian varieties with Ulrich $B^1_X \otimes L$ allowing twists by arbitrary line bundles.

papers.title: Backward Homogeneous Heat Equation with $Ψ$-Caputo Time Derivative and Spectral Fractional Laplacian
papers.abstract: In this work, we study a fractional diffusion model in time and space, formulated in an open and bounded domain, involving a Caputo fractional derivative of order $μ\in(0,1)$ with respect to a time scale function $Ψ$, together with a spectral fractional Laplacian operator of order $s\in(0,1)$. The associated direct problem is analyzed, as well as the inverse problem of temporal reconstruction from final data, which is inherently ill-posed. Through a spectral representation, the instability of the problem and the effect of the choice of the function $Ψ$ on the amplification of spectral modes are examined.

papers.title: Linear Axiomatization of Linear Differential Equations
papers.abstract: This article presents an axiomatization of linear differential equations that is complete for topologically open properties with compact initial conditions and time horizons by proving them deductively via a sound reduction to formulas of linear real arithmetic. Indeed, linearity is preserved: linear differential invariants are complete for open properties of linear differential equations and reduce with a linear number of Lie derivatives (per atom) to linear real arithmetic. In particular, this article shows that the linear fragment of differential dynamic logic (dL), a modal extension of standard first-order logic over the reals satisfies these completeness properties. By establishing completeness within decidable linear real arithmetic, the need for proving sophisticated nonlinear formulas of real arithmetic is circumvented. Furthermore, this article establishes generalizations to the nonlinear fragment of dL that enable the practical certification of reachability computations, validating the output of external computations in dL with machine-checkable proofs.

papers.title: Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.

papers.title: Hyperbolic comparison and rigidity for the hyperspherical radius
papers.abstract: We prove Gromov's hyperbolic hyperspherical radius comparison and rigidity conjectures in all dimensions $n\ge3$, without the spin assumption. Let $(X^n, g)$ be a smooth, oriented, connected, compact Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth connected boundary $S$. If ${\rm Sc}_g\ge -n(n-1)$ and $H_S\ge (n-1)\coth R$ for some $R>0$, then ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)\le\sinh R$, with equality if and only if $(X^n,g)$ is isometric to the closed hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$. Under the same curvature bounds, every smooth $1$-Lipschitz map of nonzero degree from $S$ to the boundary of the hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$ extends to an isometry of the fillings. Here, $g_S$ is the induced boundary metric, $H_S$ is the mean curvature of $S$ with respect to the outward unit normal, and ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)$ denotes the hyperspherical radius.

papers.title: Real-analytic standard families and rotational invariant curves
papers.abstract: In this paper we study one-parameter families of exact standard maps of the form $$\widehat{f}_{k,g}(\widehat{x},\widehat{y}) =\bigl(\widehat{x}+\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x}) \bmod 1,\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x})\bigr),$$ where $k$ is a real parameter and $g:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic, 1-periodic and has zero mean. The most famous example is when $g(\widehat{x})=\frac{\sin(2π\widehat{x})}{2π}$. In this case, the closed subset $A_{\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}\subset \mathbb{R}$ of values of $k$ for which $\widehat{f}_{k,\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}$ has rotational invariant curves is conjectured to be a closed interval. Much has been done towards this conjecture, both numerically and analytically. But a complete proof has not yet been achieved. Our approach here goes in the opposite direction: we construct a function $θ:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the above conditions, such that $A_θ$ is not an interval: It contains at least 2 different connected components, which are non-degenerate closed intervals.

papers.title: Borrowing Strength Across Stores: Transfer Learning for Choice-Based Revenue Management
papers.abstract: Large retail chains must tailor assortment and pricing decisions to local customer preferences, yet even retailers with extensive sales records often have limited data for estimating demand at the store or local market level, particularly in product categories with short selling windows. Local estimation (fitting a demand model for each store on its own) can therefore be unreliable, while pooling data across stores improves estimation precision at the cost of ignoring local demand heterogeneity. We study how retailers can balance these competing effects through transfer learning under a multinomial logit (MNL) demand model. We propose a shrinkage estimator that combines store-specific demand estimates with information pooled from other stores. Unlike the linear or quadratic settings underlying much of the existing theoretical literature on information transfer in operations, the nonlinear MNL likelihood does not admit a straightforward bias-variance decomposition. By exploiting its self-concordant-like properties, we establish finite-sample performance guarantees that characterize when information transfer improves demand estimation and how the appropriate degree of shrinkage depends on local sample size, feature dimensionality, and cross-store heterogeneity. We further derive regret bounds for downstream assortment and pricing decisions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the operational benefits of shrinkage across different data environments. An empirical study using data from several hundred stores of a European apparel retailer shows that shrinkage improves out-of-sample product prioritization and revenue capture relative to both local estimation and full pooling. Our findings demonstrate how retailers can leverage information across their store networks to improve revenue management decisions while preserving local demand differences.

papers.title: Homotopy Groups of Special Orthogonal Groups in Degrees 23 to 29
papers.abstract: This book presents calculations of the $2$-primary components of the homotopy groups $π_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq 28$ and all $n$, as well as some $π_{29}(\mathit{SO}(n))$, with explicit generators.

papers.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
papers.abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Zúñiga, are given.

papers.title: Scaling limits for peeling explorations of the Brownian half-plane
papers.abstract: We construct and study peeling explorations of the Brownian half-plane by successively revealing hulls of fixed radius. We prove that for any peeling process, as the radius of the hulls tends to zero, the sequence of discovered hulls converges to an explicit family of Brownian disks. We also consider the particular case of what we call nearest-neighbour peeling explorations, where the center of each new hull is chosen on the outer boundary of the previously discovered hull, naturally giving rise to an exploration curve. We provide scaling limits results for these curves, jointly with the convergence of the associated boundary-length and volume processes.

papers.title: Do Neural Models Prefer Their Submodels?
papers.abstract: A neural model is the set of functions that can be expressed by a given neural network architecture. Neural models contain natural submodels, such as those obtained by setting some neurons to be inactive. We study the geometry of neural models and ask whether they prefer their submodels. By this we mean whether local minimizers of the loss function lie in a given submodel. We introduce a geometric framework to determine if this occurs. For shallow multilayer perceptrons, we show that subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are never preferred. For deep multilayer perceptrons, we give conditions under which subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are not preferred. For lightning self-attention, lower-rank submodels are usually not preferred, but we identify examples where they are because they lie on a boundary of the model. Our results show that, aside from a few exceptions, preference for submodels cannot be explained by the geometry of the neural model, and must instead come from other sources such as training dynamics.

papers.title: Néel-vector-dependent magneto-optical and spin Hall responses in altermagnetic CrSb
papers.abstract: Altermagnets enable spin-split bands and anomalous transport phenomena with vanishing net magnetization, yet the symmetry-governed dependence of their optical and spin transport responses on the Néel-vector orientation remains largely unexplored. Using first-principles calculations and systematic ma…

papers.abstract: We present an exact solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations that describes a static black hole coexisting with anisotropic matter immersed in an external magnetic field, obtained via the Harrison transformation. papers.abstract: The crystal symmetry of Fe-deficient Fe3-xGeTe2 at room temperature has been investigated by a combination of selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) and convergent-beam electron diffraction (CBED). By symmetry analysis of CBED patterns along different zone axis, the space group of Fe3-xGeTe2 at r…

papers.abstract: Charge transfer is a fundamental process that lies at the heart of a wide variety of fields, including bioscience, physical chemistry, optoelectronics, and 2D semiconductor devices. The control of charge transfer dynamics requires localization of an initial electronic wave packet, which can be achie…

papers.abstract: In this article, we use the expression of the Schwarzian derivative to set up differential equations to find answers to three fundamental questions in the context of QFT in curved spacetime, specifically in two dimensions. One of the ways in which one can derive the Unruh effect in two dimensions is…

papers.abstract: Granular clogging at narrow constrictions is commonly described as a memoryless Poisson process, capturing the stochastic onset of clogs but not the emergence of mechanically stable arches. papers.abstract: Arguably, the lamp-pumped vapor-cell atomic clock is the workhorse of precise timekeeping in space. However, the present-day Rb atomic frequency standard (RAFS) has two clear deficiencies: (1) its short-term stability is limited by weak optical pumping, and (2) its long-term stability can be limited…

papers.abstract: Using the magnetostatic approximation, we calculate the spectra of bulk and surface spin waves in an in-plane magnetized ferromagnet/paramagnet bilayer. papers.abstract: Uncovering hidden structural dynamics in an organic conductor Organic conductors host a remarkable interplay between molecular structure and electronic properties. In \kappa-(BETS)2Mn(N(CN)2)3, a multiferroic candidate exhibiting electronic ferroelectricity below the metal-to-insulator transition at 25 K, we identify the microscopic origin of a long-standing anomaly near 100 K. Resistance noise spectroscopy, thermal expansion, and computational modeling reveal compelling evidence for a glass-like freezing of dicyanamide ligands in the anion layer. Despite occurring outside the conducting layer, this structural transition leaves a pronounced fingerprint on the charge-carrier dynamics. Our results demonstrate that slow structural fluctuations in the anion network can strongly influence electronic behavior, providing new insight into the role of donor-anion coupling and disorder in organic quantum materials.
